mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and increasing the present value of S&P 500 earnings, leading to positive forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average return in such periods is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% over a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, increasing recession risk and prompting equity investors to demand higher risk premiums, resulting in negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.0% in a month, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals weakening aggregate demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and triggering negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 92.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, signaling a weakening economy and reducing corporate profitability, which leads to negative forward 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains above 2.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment that raises discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of high FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in residential construction (HOUST) above 570.0 thousand units, following two consecutive months of decline, signals a recovery in housing demand, boosting confidence in the broader economy and driving positive forward 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 131,000 thousand persons for three consecutive months signals strong labor market demand, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives positive forward 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 131,000 for three months, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months, combined with a decline in residential construction (HOUST), indicates a deepening demand-side recession, leading to negative forward 20-day S&P 500 returns due to falling earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
